about: The lenses a seat wears when it challenges other seats. room.py deals one lens per seat per challenge round: never the seat's native lens, never one it already wore, cynical and client-eyes in every round, and the rest spread evenly. Every challenge must fill in the lens's test. Edit freely; keep ids unique.

lenses.name: Analytical
lenses.stance: Only numbers that add up survive. Follow every figure back to the brief, the data or a stated assumption, and redo the arithmetic.
lenses.test: The one number that must be true for this plan to work, where it comes from, and whether it holds.

lenses.name: Cynical
lenses.stance: Assume the plan is lying to itself. Look for the optimistic assumption, the missing owner, the step nobody has done before.
lenses.test: The most likely way this fails in real life, and the earliest warning sign that it is failing.

lenses.name: Business
lenses.stance: Judge it as the client's CFO would. Revenue, margin, payback, CAC against LTV, and the cost of being wrong.
lenses.test: What this does to the client's money: cost, return, payback, and what happens if it underdelivers by 30%.

lenses.name: Operations
lenses.stance: Plans die in handoffs. Count hours, people, lead times, approvals and the order things must happen in.
lenses.test: Who does it, how many hours, what it waits on, and the date it is really ready.

lenses.name: Client eyes
lenses.stance: Read it as the client's marketing director reading it cold, with their boss, their politics and their approval chain.
lenses.test: What the client will push back on or refuse to sign, and what they will ask in the first meeting.

lenses.name: Customer
lenses.stance: Be the person who sees the ad on their phone and has three seconds and no patience.
lenses.test: The moment the end customer drops off or feels misled, from the ad to the page to the form.

lenses.name: Brand
lenses.stance: Protect what the brand means in a year, not just this quarter's numbers. Consistency, distinctiveness, trust.
lenses.test: Where this makes the brand look inconsistent, generic or cheap, and what that costs later.

lenses.name: Risk & compliance
lenses.stance: Platform policy, privacy law, consent, claims, regulated categories, brand safety. Assume someone will check.
lenses.test: The rule, policy or law this could break (name it), and what happens if it does: a rejected ad, a banned account, a fine.

lenses.name: Competitive
lenses.stance: The client is not alone in the auction. Think about who else bids, what they say and how they will react.
lenses.test: What the strongest competitor does in response, and whether this plan still wins after that.

lenses.name: Opportunity
lenses.stance: Look for the upside nobody has claimed: the cheaper channel, the reusable asset, the audience left out.
lenses.test: The biggest upside this plan leaves on the table, with a rough size for it.
